labels.rationale: Spread is a segment-coverage composition artifact, not travel-time variability. The cell's percentiles are taken over only 6 hourly aggregate rows (one per hour-of-day in the daypart), and the 'runtime' is a SUM of average_travel_time_minutes across a varying number of segment rows per hour (21-36 rows): row-count buffer index 0.595 explains most of the runtime buffer index 1.21, with per-row spread only 0.374. The claim text also publishes P50 198.9 min as a route runtime, which is not a plausible trip runtime. The reported observedTripCount 2455 is a segment-row trip sum, not the percentile sample size.

Only emitted cell family where the spread survives composition decomposition: per-row runtime buffer index 0.955 vs segment-row-count buffer index 0.179 across 10 hourly samples. But the spread is across hours of day inside the off_peak band (which mixes overnight and evening service), not across days or trips, and the claim's P50 349.1 min is a sum over non-unique segment cells, not a trip runtime. A real B35 off-peak variability story may exist; it needs trip-level runtime distributions and a daypart decomposition before any public use.
